rationale: The V2.1 word-pair anchors are abstract nominal phrases ('captured institutions', 'public agenda control'). Under inspection the P channel fires on mainstream participatory-democracy rhetoric and the M channel fires on professions of virtue, because both name the concept rather than the assertion. These anchors state each channel as a first-person political claim of the kind a speaker actually makes, so the axis separates asserting the populist proposition from asserting its mainstream alternative.
construct_source: Ideational definition of populism: people-centrism, anti-elitism, and Manichean moral antagonism.

P.label: people sovereignty
populist: The ordinary people are the only true source of legitimate political power.
It is the people, not the officials, who must decide the future of this country.
We are here to give the country back to the people it belongs to.
The will of the ordinary citizen must come before the preferences of any institution.
Nobody has the right to overrule what the people have decided.
This movement is nothing more and nothing less than the voice of ordinary people.
Power must be returned to the hands of the people who built this nation.
The common people know perfectly well what is good for them.
Our people are sovereign and no authority stands above them.
What the ordinary working family wants is what this government will do.
mainstream: Complex policy questions require careful analysis by qualified specialists.
Our constitutional institutions provide the proper framework for these decisions.
This government will follow the recommendations of the independent commission.
Sound policy is developed through deliberation among many stakeholders.
We must respect the procedures that our legal system prescribes.
Expert advice has guided our approach throughout this process.
The relevant ministries have reviewed the evidence and issued their guidance.
Representative institutions exist precisely to weigh these competing interests.
We will proceed in accordance with established regulatory practice.
A technical assessment will determine the appropriate course of action.

E.label: elite obstruction
populist: A corrupt elite has captured our institutions and turned them against the public.
The establishment in the capital works only for itself and its donors.
Bankers, lobbyists and career politicians have rigged the system against you.
A small privileged clique makes every decision behind closed doors.
The people in power have betrayed the country they were elected to serve.
Entrenched insiders block every reform that would help ordinary families.
They enrich themselves while the rest of the country is told to sacrifice.
An unelected bureaucracy overrules whatever the voters ask for.
The political class protects its own privileges above everything else.
Powerful interests have bought the influence that should belong to citizens.
mainstream: Our public servants have worked diligently to implement this programme.
The agency has met its obligations and reported transparently on its work.
Officials across government cooperated effectively on this initiative.
The civil service continues to deliver essential services to the public.
Regulators acted within their mandate and published their findings.
Members of this chamber have debated the proposal in good faith.
The commission consulted widely before publishing its recommendations.
Our institutions have proved resilient and accountable in difficult times.
Public bodies are subject to audit and parliamentary oversight.
The department has responded constructively to the concerns raised.

M.label: moralized antagonism
populist: This is a battle between honest people and a thoroughly corrupt establishment.
They lie to your face and they have been lying for decades.
These people are not merely mistaken, they are morally rotten.
It is time to drain the swamp and throw out the crooks.
Their greed and their treachery have brought this country to its knees.
We are the decent ones and they are the parasites feeding on us.
Everything they say is a fraud designed to deceive ordinary citizens.
They have sold out the nation for their own miserable profit.
There can be no compromise with people this dishonest.
Their corruption is not an accident, it is who they are.
mainstream: Reasonable people can disagree about the best way forward.
I want to acknowledge the constructive contribution of the opposition.
We should seek common ground wherever it can honestly be found.
My colleagues hold a different view and they argue it sincerely.
This is a difficult trade-off with legitimate arguments on both sides.
I thank the honourable member for raising a serious point.
Our disagreements are real but they are conducted in good faith.
Let us debate the substance rather than question anyone's motives.
Both parties share a commitment to the wellbeing of this country.
We will continue to work with all sides to reach a durable agreement.
